chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hallal, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:

I said to Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام: What do you say regarding the blood of fleas? He said: There is no harm in it. He said: I said: It becomes abundant. He said: Even if it is abundant. He said: I said: Then if a man has spots of blood on his garment and does not know about it, then he comes to know of it but forgets to wash it and so he performs salat (prayer), then remembers after he has prayed, should he repeat his salat (prayer)? He said: He should wash it and not repeat his salat (prayer), unless it is gathered together to the amount of a dirham; then he should wash it and repeat the salat (prayer).

key_terms.دَمِ الْبَرَاغِيثِ: the blood of fleas, discussed here as excused impurity
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: there is no harm in it; it is not treated as problematic here
key_terms.مُجْتَمِعًا: gathered together or combined in one total amount
key_terms.مِقْدَارَ الدِّرْهَمِ: the amount of a dirham, used here as a legal threshold
key_terms.نُقَطُ الدَّمِ: small spots of blood on a garment

ai.seo_question: Does blood on clothing invalidate salat (prayer), and what is the ruling on flea blood?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on blood found on clothing in relation to salat (prayer). It states that the blood of fleas is excused even if abundant, and that forgotten blood on a garment does not require repeating the prayer unless it had reached the combined amount of a dirham.
